note: Window agent p1970-p1979, 2 Nov 2026. Events 0-2: the Egypt ledger's partial occupation_end events close Israel's whole occupation, so the Sinai (held to 1982) is re-marked; 3: the Halaib cells go to Sudan; 4-5: the Saguia el-Hamra is claimed by the SADR and marked Moroccan-occupied; 6: Barentu to Ethiopia; 7: seven Sakhalin/Kuril cells to the USSR; 8-10: the Golan (unowned in the 1970 anchor) is Syrian land occupied by Israel. No keyframe_overrides and no rulings: the border registration differences of Cliopatria shapes are reported, not patched. Reviewed 2 Nov 2026: events/9 month 6 -> 12, events/7 slug -> the RSFSR, events/4 counterpart -> kingdom-of-spain. Seam agent sm-08, 2 Nov 2026: events 11-18 repair the Western Sahara partition under the current dossiers (francoist-spain/ledger/10 gives the whole territory to Morocco): 11-12 the republic owns the territory and the Free Zone is contested; 13 Morocco's 47 northern Oued ed-Dahab cells; 14-15 Mauritania's Tiris from April 1976; 16-18 the Tiris after August 1979 (west of the berm occupied by Morocco, east of it contested). Events 4-5 stay as they were.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula east of the Suez Canal strip: Israel withdrew only 'from immediate proximity with the Suez Canal'

events.note: After the October 1973 war Israel still held the Sinai: the Egypt ledger's occupation_end events (6 Oct 1973, 1974, 1975) each close the whole Israeli occupation, though they release only the canal strip. The Sinai page: 'Israel withdrew from immediate proximity with the Suez Canal' and only 'In 1982 ... Israel withdrew from all of the Sinai Peninsula'. Re-opens the occupation of the rest of the Sinai.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula east of the Suez Canal strip: Israel withdrew only 'from immediate proximity with the Suez Canal'

events.note: The dossier's 1974 occupation_end (the west bank of the canal) closes the pair's whole occupation again; the Sinai east of the canal strip stayed Israeli until 1982 ('In 1982, as a result of the Egypt-Israel peace treaty of 1979, Israel withdrew from all of the Sinai Peninsula').

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula outside the immediate Suez Canal area

events.note: The 1975 occupation_end (Israel leaves the canal area, 'The canal was reopened in 1975') closes the pair's whole occupation; the rest of the Sinai stays Israeli to 1982 (the 1979 treaty: 'Israel agreed to withdraw from the entirety of the Sinai Peninsula'). Until the dossier's own 1982 occupation_end.

region.text: the Halaib Triangle with Abu Ramad and Shalateen's coast, the 86 cells the Egypt dossier cuts from its shape

events.note: The Egypt dossier cuts the Halaib Triangle out of Egypt from 1971 (and the United Arab Republic's shape holds it in 1970) but no dossier gives it to Sudan, so 86 cells stay owned by nobody until 1994. The Halaib Triangle page: 'Sudan held to the 1902 administrative boundary'; Egypt's troops sent in February 1958 were withdrawn 'the same month'; 'joint control of the area remained in effect until 1992'; 'the Egyptian military moved to take control of the area' in 1994. So Sudan administers it through the 1970s.

union.text: the Saguia el-Hamra and the northern part of the territory that Morocco took over
the northern part of the former Spanish Sahara inside the gazetteer's Guelmim - Es-Semara unit (Smara and the Saguia el-Hamra south of 27.67 N)

region.text: the Saguia el-Hamra: the Laayoune-Boujdour unit and the Smara part the gazetteer files under Guelmim - Es-Semara

events.note: The SADR keyframe takes the Laayoune-Boujdour and Oued el Dahab units and the Free Zone but not the Smara part of the Saguia el-Hamra, which the gazetteer files under Guelmim - Es-Semara; the 128 Smara cells stay owned by nobody from the Spanish withdrawal. Claiming the whole Saguia el-Hamra here (the keyframe is applied at year end) lets the Moroccan occupation of the next entry mark it. The Western Sahara War page: 'On 26 February 1976, Spain officially announced its full withdrawal from the area', 'The Polisario Front proclaimed the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic on 27 February 1976', 'Morocco took over the Saguia El Hamra and the northern two-thirds of the territory'. (Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: counterpart kingdom-of-spain, not francoist-spain, which ends in November 1975.)

union.text: the Saguia el-Hamra and the northern part of the territory that Morocco took over
the northern part of the former Spanish Sahara inside the gazetteer's Guelmim - Es-Semara unit (Smara and the Saguia el-Hamra south of 27.67 N)

region.text: the Saguia el-Hamra and the northern two-thirds of Western Sahara that Morocco took over in 1976

events.note: 1976: 'Morocco took over the Saguia El Hamra and the northern two-thirds of the territory' (Western Sahara War page; 'Morocco controls approximately 80% of the territory'). The SADR dossier's own occupation_start for Morocco is applied before its land exists and so marks nothing; this marks the Moroccan-held north as occupied. The month (3) only orders it after the SADR's founding in month 2; the page gives no month for the takeover.

region.text: Barentu, given as a coordinate (the gazetteer lacks the name)

events.note: The EPLF 1977 keyframe cuts Barentu out of the EPLF's land but nothing gives it to Ethiopia, so 21 cells stay owned by nobody. The Eritrean War of Independence page: 'All of Eritrea was liberated with the exception of Asmara, Massawa, Assab and Barentu'; the EPLF 'expelled the Ethiopians from the town of Barentu' only in the summer of 1985.

union.text: the Korsakov end of south Sakhalin

region.text: seven cells of south Sakhalin, Tyuleniy Island and Iturup that the 1970 anchor still has under Japan

events.note: The 1970 anchor leaves seven Sakhalin and Kuril cells with Japan. The Kuril Islands dispute page: 'The Soviet Union invaded South Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands' in 1945, the 1956 promise of Habomai and Shikotan was conditional on a peace treaty that was never concluded, and the islands are 'under Russian administration as the South Kuril District'; Japan claims them but has not held them since 1945. (Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: given to the RSFSR, whose ledger gains southern Sakhalin and the Kurils from Japan in September 1945 and which holds the neighbouring cells as a USSR constituent, not to the USSR directly.)

The Golan cells are owned by nobody in the 1970 anchor, so Israel's own 1967 occupation_start (recorded by Israel, over land Syria does not hold) is read the wrong way round and marks nothing. The Golan Heights page: 'the Israel Defense Forces captured the Golan Heights on 9-10 June' 1967; in 1974 the arrangement 'left almost all the Heights in Israeli hands'. Gives the land to Syria so that Israel's occupation can mark it. The Ba'ath Party dossier's own keyframe is meant to hold the Golan, but the 1970 anchor has the seven cells unowned.

Israel holds the Golan Heights taken from Syria on 9-10 June 1967 through the 1970s (1974: the disengagement 'left almost all the Heights in Israeli hands'; 14 December 1981: the Golan Heights Law). Re-states the 1967 occupation over land Syria now holds in the compile. The month only orders it after Syria's gain (reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: was 6; events/8 has no month and takes 11 from the Ba'ath dossier's November 1970 rename, so at month 6 the Golan was still nobody's and the occupation was read the wrong way round, marking two Israeli cells as occupied by Syria).

The Ba'ath Party row of Syria ends in 1972 and 'syria' takes over the same cells in 1973, which closes the occupation of the previous entry. Israel still held the Golan after the October 1973 war ('Syrian forces overran much of the southern Golan, before being pushed back by an Israeli counterattack'; 1974: 'left almost all the Heights in Israeli hands'; 14 December 1981: the Golan Heights Law). The month only orders it after the October entries.

region.text: the whole former Spanish Sahara, the 266,000 km2 the republic claims

events.note: Seam sm-08, replacing events/4 (which now moves nothing). The Western Sahara War page: Spain 'ceded the administrative control of the territory to Mauritania and Morocco on 14 November 1975' and 'On 26 February 1976, Spain officially announced its full withdrawal'; the republic page: proclaimed 27 February 1976 at Bir Lehlou, '266,000 km2 (claimed)', and it 'controls the rest of the territory that lies to the east of the Moroccan-built Berm'. francoist-spain/ledger/10 now hands the whole territory (975 cells) to Morocco, and morocco/ledger/23-25 name only the gazetteer's 'Western Sahara' (the Free Zone), so on 1 January 1976 Morocco holds all of it and events/4, a gain from a Spain that holds none of it, takes nothing. The republic owns the territory by its claim (its keyframe, as events/4-5 and the p2020-p2029 entries have it); the Moroccan and Mauritanian holds are drawn by the entries that follow.

region.text: the Free Zone, the part of Western Sahara east of the Moroccan-built Berm

events.note: Seam sm-08. sahrawi-arab-democratic-republic/ledger/3 opens the war with Morocco in February 1976 before the republic holds any land, so it marked Morocco's land as contested with the republic as claimant (the Free Zone drawn Moroccan until 1991). Now that events/11 makes the republic the holder, this re-marks the Free Zone as the republic's land contested by Morocco, until the ceasefire (ledger/8). The Western Sahara War page: 'A ceasefire came into effect on 6 September 1991'; the berm page: the republic controls the 'Free Zone', 'all areas east of the barrier'.

region.text: the Oued ed-Dahab unit north of 24 N (47 cells): Morocco's share outside the Mauritanian Tiris

events.note: Seam sm-08. The Western Sahara page: 'Western Sahara was partitioned between Morocco and Mauritania in April 1976'; the Western Sahara War page: 'Morocco took over the Saguia El Hamra and the northern two-thirds of the territory', 'Mauritania took control of the southern third'. events/5 marks the Laayoune-Boujdour unit and the Smara part; the 47 cells of the Oued ed-Dahab unit that lie north of the Tiris (north of 24 N) were left out, so they stayed the republic's, unoccupied, until 2020. They belong to the northern two-thirds.

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro': the southern third of Western Sahara

events.note: Seam sm-08. April 1976: 'Western Sahara was partitioned between Morocco and Mauritania' (Western Sahara page); 'Mauritania took control of the southern third' (Western Sahara War page). mauritania/ledger/2 takes the Tiris from francoist-spain, which ended in November 1975 and whose land francoist-spain/ledger/10 gave to Morocco, so it took nothing and the Mauritanian share was never drawn (the mauritania_1976 keyframe found the Tiris 'kept by others'). events/11 makes the republic the holder; this takes the Tiris from it for Mauritania, as the partition did.

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro'

events.note: Seam sm-08. mauritania/ledger/1 opens the contest with 'Polisario Front', which has no dossier, so it marks nothing; the republic's ledger/4 opens the same war in February 1976 but before Mauritania holds the land. Marks the Tiris as Mauritanian land contested by the republic until the peace treaty: 'A comprehensive peace treaty was signed on 5 August 1979' (the republic's ledger/5 closes the contest).

region.text: Tiris al-Gharbiya, 'roughly corresponding to the southern half of Rio de Oro'

events.note: Seam sm-08. After the peace treaty of 5 August 1979 Mauritania 'abandoned all claims to its portion in August 1979' (Western Sahara page) and the Tiris 'was unilaterally annexed by Morocco on 11 August 1979' (Western Sahara War page). mauritania/ledger/3 gives the Tiris (401 cells) to Morocco as Moroccan land, and sahrawi-arab-democratic-republic/ledger/7 is then read as the republic occupying Moroccan land (226 cells drawn 'Morocco, occupied by the SADR'; the 175 cells east of the berm Moroccan outright until 1991). The land is the republic's by its claim, like the rest of the territory; the next two entries mark what Morocco held and what it only claimed.

region.text: the Tiris west of the berm (226 cells, Dakhla and the coast), which Morocco took over in August 1979

events.note: Seam sm-08. The Tiris 'was unilaterally annexed by Morocco on 11 August 1979' (Western Sahara War page); the berm page: the fifth stage (May-September 1985) enclosed 'Guelta Zemmur, Bir Anzarane and Dakhla', and Morocco controls the land west of the wall. With the republic holding the land (previous entry), Morocco is the occupier: the same relation as events/5.

region.text: the part of the Tiris inside the Free Zone, east of the berm (175 cells)

events.note: Seam sm-08. The Moroccan annexation of the Tiris in August 1979 was a claim over the part east of the later berm, which Morocco never held: the berm page gives the republic the 'Free Zone', 'all areas east of the barrier', and the Western Sahara page '30% ... controlled by the Polisario Front'. Marks these cells as the republic's land contested by Morocco, like the rest of the Free Zone (the contest of events/12, closed by ledger/8 in 1991).
